cases.expected: The role list shows “Operations User”, “Support User”, “Accountant”, “Operations Manager” and “Support Manager” between “Chartered Accountant” and Operator. After the save (with four-eye ON: after the second admin approves) the user holds the three roles. The role switcher lists “Accountant”, “Support” and “Operations”; each switch lands on /staff, and the header board link points to /staff (it is labelled “Operator board”).

cases.title: Accountant is only the maker and the CA only the checker
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_accounting` ON (Admin → Feature flags; seeded OFF). gk-ops acting as Accountant, gk-oplim acting as CA.
cases.expected: Steps 1–4 answer 403 “You do not have permission to perform this action.” and nothing is created or changed. Step 5 opens Finance read-only for the Accountant: no settlement prepare / pay / refund controls (the role holds finance view and payment view only).

cases.title: Support User and Support Manager cannot write shop data or change roles
cases.preconditions: gk-oplim acting as Support User, gk-ops acting as Support Manager; shop A of the staging world.
cases.expected: Steps 1 and 3 answer 403 “This shop does not belong to you.”; step 2 redirects to / (the full queue needs the help-desk manage permission); step 4 answers 403 “You do not have permission to perform this action.”. The shop and the role are unchanged; each refusal adds an authz.denied audit row. Support changes reach a shop only as change requests (TS-STAFF-10).

cases.title: Operations User onboards shops through the Operator (Limited) flow, own shops only
cases.preconditions: gk-oplim switched to Operations User (works with every rbac_v2_* flag OFF); a shop owner ready to read back the consent code; a live shop this user did not onboard.
cases.steps:
1. Open /operator
2. Open /operator/onboard and onboard a shop with the owner's consent code
3. Open /operator/shops
4. PATCH /api/shops/{a shop this user onboarded} {description: “QA”}
cases.expected: The onboarding board opens for the Operations User (it redirected to /admin before PR #485) and onboarding works exactly as for Operator (Limited), consent code and fee included; My shops lists only shops this user onboarded. Step 4 answers 403 “This shop does not belong to you.” — approved shop data is changed only through a ticket to Support.

cases.title: Existing roles keep all their access
cases.preconditions: Accounts acting as CA, Operator, Operator (Limited) and shop owner.
cases.steps:
1. As CA open /admin/statutory and /admin/tds-commission
2. As CA open /admin/finance and /staff
3. As Operator open /admin and approve a pending shop
4. As Operator (Limited) open /operator and /staff
5. As shop owner open /shop/prices
cases.expected: Everything that worked before still works (nothing was removed from CA, Operator, Operator (Limited) or shop owner). The CA additionally opens /admin/finance (read-only) and the staff board /staff (its role-switcher home). /staff sends the Operator to /admin and Operator (Limited) to /.

cases.title: Operations Manager and Accountant stay out of each other's areas
cases.preconditions: All rbac_v2_* area flags ON; gk-ops switching between Operations Manager and Accountant.
cases.steps:
1. As Operations Manager open /admin/finance, /admin/support and /staff/accounting
2. As Operations Manager GET /api/approvals
3. As Accountant open /staff/operations
4. As Accountant open /staff/support?tab=dashboard
cases.expected: /admin/finance and /admin/support redirect to /; /staff/accounting and (for the Accountant) /staff/operations redirect to /staff; GET /api/approvals answers 403. The Accountant's /staff/support shows only the tabs “Raised by me” and “Raise a ticket” (no Dashboard or Queue) and the dashboard parameter falls back to the raised list.

cases.title: Each staff role sees only its own tiles on /staff
cases.preconditions: All six rbac_v2_* flags ON with no role scope; gk-ops and gk-oplim, switching roles in the header.
cases.steps:
1. Switch to CA and open /staff
2. Repeat as Accountant, Support Manager, Support User, Operations Manager and Operations User
3. Open each tile's menu and read the entries
cases.expected: Title “My work” with the role line. CA: Finance, Tax and statutory, Accounting (Journal entries, Periods, To approve, Trial balance, Rate changes, Bank reconciliation), Raise a ticket. Accountant: Finance, Accounting without “To approve”, Raise a ticket. Support Manager: Support queue (All tickets, Disputes, Team workload), Raise a ticket. Support User: My work (My tickets, Changes sent to owners), Raise a ticket. Operations Manager: Operations team (Tasks, Team & zones, Onboarding reports, Customers), Raise a ticket. Operations User: Onboard a shop (Onboard, My shops, Documents), Operations team (My day, Tasks, Customers), Raise a ticket. Raise a ticket holds “Raise to Support”, “Raised by me” and “My help tickets”. No role sees another role's tile.

cases.title: Each role's desk opens with its area flag on
cases.preconditions: All six rbac_v2_* flags ON; gk-ops, gk-oplim and an admin.
cases.steps:
1. As Accountant open /staff/accounting?tab=bank
2. As CA open /staff/accounting?tab=approvals
3. As Support Manager open /staff/support
4. As Operations Manager open /staff/operations
5. As Operations User open /staff
6. As Admin open /admin/approvals and /admin/staff-teams
cases.expected: Each page answers 200 and renders without “Application error”. Accounting shows the tabs Journals, To approve, Periods, Rates, Bank, Trial balance; the Support desk opens on Dashboard; Operations opens on Overview; Approvals and Staff teams render for the admin.

cases.title: /staff sends everyone who is not staff elsewhere
cases.preconditions: Accounts acting as Customer, shop owner, Operator (Limited), Admin and Operator.
cases.steps:
1. Open /staff signed out
2. Open /staff as Customer
3. As shop owner
4. As Operator (Limited)
5. As Admin and as Operator
cases.expected: Guest → /signin; Customer, shop owner and Operator (Limited) → / (they do not hold the staff board permission); Admin and Operator → /admin. No staff tile or data is shown to any of them.

cases.title: Area tiles follow their flags; rbac_v2_staff_roles alone does not hide the board
cases.preconditions: Flags `rbac_v2_accounting`, `rbac_v2_support`, `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests`, `rbac_v2_operations` and `rbac_v2_staff_roles` OFF (seeded OFF; ON on staging since 23-Nov — switch off with a second admin if four-eye is on).
cases.steps:
1. As Accountant open /staff
2. As Support User open /staff
3. As Operations User open /staff
4. Switch `rbac_v2_accounting` ON and reload /staff as Accountant
cases.expected: With the area flags off there is no Accounting, My work or Operations team tile and no “Raise to Support” / “Raised by me” entry. Tiles without a flag still show: Finance (Accountant), Onboard a shop (Operations User) and Raise a ticket → “My help tickets”; the Support User sees only Raise a ticket. /staff itself still opens although `rbac_v2_staff_roles` is OFF — the code never reads that flag (see code_check). After step 4 the Accounting tile appears.

cases.title: Staff screens on a phone
cases.preconditions: 375 × 812 viewport; area flags ON; one bank statement and one pending change request exist.
cases.steps:
1. Open /staff for a staff role
2. Open /staff/accounting?tab=tb and a bank statement (?tab=bank&statement=…)
3. Open /staff/support?tab=queue as Support Manager
4. Open /staff/operations?tab=reports as Operations Manager
5. Open /shop/changes as the shop owner
cases.expected: The tile board fits one screen; tab rows wrap; trial balance, change-item and breakdown tables scroll inside their card; long narrations and references wrap; no sideways scroll of the page; buttons and tab links are at least 44 px high.

cases.title: Android and iOS apps open /staff links inside the app
cases.preconditions: Android APK built after PR #485 (app-link prefix /staff) and the iOS app; staff account; a task-assigned e-mail with a /staff/operations/tasks/{id} link.
cases.steps:
1. On Android tap the /staff link in the e-mail
2. Do the same on iOS
3. Sign in and use the staff board and the task page
cases.expected: Both open the page inside the GoKesari app (Android only from the APK built after #485 — an older APK opens the browser; iOS opens every path). The WebView shows the same tiles and actions as the website. Tracker status for mobile: “Deployed, not run”.

cases.title: A refused check writes one authz.denied row; the response is unchanged; at most 20 a minute
cases.preconditions: gk-oplim acting as Support User; admin with the audit log (/admin/console/audit-log).
cases.steps:
1. As Support User: GET /api/approvals
2. As Admin: open the audit log and find action authz.denied
3. As Support User: repeat step 1 25 times within one minute
4. Count that user's authz.denied rows for that minute
cases.expected: Each call answers 403 “You do not have permission to perform this action.” (same as before PR #485). One authz.denied row per refusal: actor, role SUPPORT_USER, entity type “permission”, entity id “approval:view:any|journal:approve”. At most 20 rows for the user in one minute per server process; the other calls are still refused but not logged. Works with every flag OFF.

cases.title: The six rbac_v2_* flags on Admin → Feature flags
cases.preconditions: Admin; a database freshly migrated to 0170 (local) for the default state.
cases.steps:
1. Open /admin/feature-flags
2. Read the six RBAC v2 rows and their hints
3. On the fresh database check their state
4. Change one flag with the reason “QA” and then with a reason of 5+ characters
cases.expected: Rows: “Staff roles: CA, Accountant, Support and Operations boards”, “Two-admin approval for user, role, suspension and flag changes”, “Accounting: journal entries, period close, rate proposals”, “Support desk: manager queue and Support Users”, “Support-proposed shop changes approved by the shop owner”, “Operations: tasks, zones, onboarding reports”. Migration 0170 seeds all six OFF. Reason “QA” → “Say why you are changing this flag.”; a valid reason saves (or, with four-eye ON, sends for approval) and is logged with who, old, new and reason.

cases.title: Each back-office area is hidden and refused while its flag is OFF
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_accounting`, `rbac_v2_support`, `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests` and `rbac_v2_operations` OFF; staff accounts with the roles; shop owner of shop A.
cases.steps:
1. As Accountant open /staff/accounting and GET /api/staff/accounting/journals
2. As Support Manager open /staff/support and POST /api/staff/support/tickets for shop A
3. As Support User POST /api/staff/shops/{shopA}/changes
4. As Operations Manager open /staff/operations and GET /api/staff/operations/tasks
5. As shop owner open Price updates and /shop/changes
cases.expected: /staff/accounting, /staff/support and /staff/operations redirect to /staff; /shop/changes redirects to /shop and Price updates has no “Pending changes” entry. The APIs answer 404 “This feature is not available.” and nothing is created. The rest of the site works as before.

cases.title: A flag's role scope limits the area to the named roles
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_accounting` ON. There is no admin screen for the role scope (code_check): the developer sets feature_flags.role_scope = '{ACCOUNTANT}' for that key and the flag cache expires (or the app restarts).
cases.steps:
1. As Accountant open /staff/accounting
2. As CA open /staff and /staff/accounting
3. As CA GET /api/staff/accounting/journals
4. Developer sets role_scope back to NULL; repeat step 2
cases.expected: Accountant works normally. For the CA the Accounting tile is hidden, /staff/accounting redirects to /staff and the API answers 404 “This feature is not available.”. With role_scope NULL both roles work again.

cases.title: Admin → Approvals: who opens it and what it shows
cases.preconditions: Admin; CA, Operator and Customer accounts.
cases.steps:
1. As Admin open Settings → Approvals (/admin/approvals) with `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` OFF
2. Open it with the flag ON and nothing pending
3. Open it as CA, Operator and Customer
4. Open it signed out
cases.expected: Title “Approvals”, description “Changes one admin made that wait for a second admin: roles, suspensions, reactivations and feature flags. You cannot approve your own request.”. Flag OFF: info alert “Two-admin approval is off (flag rbac_v2_four_eye_admin). Admin changes apply at once, as before.”. Nothing pending: “Nothing waiting” / “No approval requests are pending.”. With fewer than two active admins a warning “Fewer than two admins are active, so the Super Admin may approve alone. …”. CA, Operator and Customer → /; guest → /signin.

cases.title: Approval requests are visible only to admins, the requester and CA checkers
cases.preconditions: At least one admin-checked request (e.g. a pending flag change) and one journal approval request exist.
cases.expected: Admin sees every request; the CA sees only CA and CA-then-admin requests; Support User 403. Step 4 → 403 “You cannot see this request.”. Step 5 returns the request with its items and decision history for both.

cases.title: Rejecting needs a comment, only the requester cancels, a decided request is final
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B; a pending request raised by Admin A.
cases.expected: 1 → “Say why you are rejecting.” on the card (422); 2 → 403 “Only the person who raised this request can cancel it.”; 3 → 403 “Cancel your own request instead of rejecting it.”; 4 → “Request cancelled.”, status CANCELLED, nothing applied; 5 → 409 “This request has already been decided.”.

cases.title: The decision history is complete and append-only
cases.preconditions: A request approved and applied (TC-STAFF-022); database access for the developer.
cases.steps:
1. GET /api/approvals/{id}
2. Read the audit log for the request
3. In psql: UPDATE approval_decisions SET comment = 'x' WHERE request_id = '{id}'
4. DELETE FROM approval_decisions WHERE request_id = '{id}'
cases.expected: Decisions SUBMIT → APPROVE → APPLY, each with actor, role and time; audit rows approval.submitted, approval.decided, approval.applied. Steps 3 and 4 fail with “approval_decisions is append-only: UPDATE is not allowed” / “… DELETE is not allowed”; nothing changes.

cases.title: A change that fails when applied is recorded as FAILED, nothing half-applied
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B; a user who is ACTIVE (not suspended).
cases.expected: Step 1 answers 202 {pendingApproval: true, approvalId, message} — with the flag ON the request is accepted at once (with it OFF, TC-ADM-018 answers 409). After approval the card says “Approved, but applying it failed: …” with the reinstate error; status FAILED with that error, decision APPLY_FAILED; the user is unchanged.

cases.title: A privileges change waits for a second admin
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON (seeded OFF; ON on staging since the 23-Nov run); two active admins (Admin A, Admin B); a test customer.
cases.steps:
1. Admin A opens /admin/users/{id}/privileges, adds Support User, saves and confirms
2. Read the message and reload the page
3. Admin B opens /admin/approvals
4. Admin B clicks “Approve” on “Set privileges: active …; holds …”
5. Reload the user's privileges
cases.expected: Step 1: “Sent for approval. A different admin must approve this before it takes effect (Admin → Approvals).”; the form returns to the saved roles and nothing changes. Admin B's card shows requester, IST time, type USER_PRIVILEGES_SET and “Reason: Privileges change”. Approve → “Approved and applied.” and the user now holds Support User. With the flag OFF, TC-RBAC-009 / TC-RBAC-010 still save at once.

cases.title: Nobody approves their own request
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; two active admins; Admin A is not the Super Admin.
cases.expected: Step 1 answers 202 with the approval id; the role is unchanged. Admin A's card shows the badge “Your request” and only “Cancel request” (no Approve). Step 3 → 403 “A different admin must approve this request.” (the Super Admin gets “A different admin must approve this request (two admins are active).”).

cases.title: With four-eye on an admin cannot change their own role, roles or privileges
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A.
cases.expected: 403 “You cannot change your own role.”, “You cannot change your own roles.” and “You cannot change your own privileges.”; no approval request is created.

cases.title: Role removal and reactivation wait for the second admin
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B; a user acting as Operator; a SUSPENDED user.
cases.steps:
1. Admin A DELETE /api/users/{operator}/roles?role=OPERATOR
2. The user reloads /admin
3. Admin B approves “Remove role OPERATOR”; the user reloads
4. Admin A POST /api/users/{suspended}/reinstate {reason: “Appeal accepted”}
5. Admin B approves “Reactivate account”; the user signs in
cases.expected: Step 1 → 202; the user keeps Operator until the approval (TC-RBAC-013's fall-back to CUSTOMER happens only after step 3), then loses the console. Step 4 → 202, the user stays suspended; after step 5 the account is ACTIVE and can sign in.

cases.title: Flag changes, including switching four-eye off, need a second admin
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B.
cases.steps:
1. Admin A PUT /api/admin/feature-flags {key: rbac_v2_operations, enabled: true, districtCodes: null, reason: “QA”}
2. Admin A switches `rbac_v2_operations` on /admin/feature-flags with the reason “QA pilot run” and saves
3. Admin A switches `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` OFF with a reason
4. Admin B approves “Switch on rbac_v2_operations” and “Switch off rbac_v2_four_eye_admin”
cases.expected: 1 → 422 “Say why you are changing this flag.”. 2 → “Sent for approval. A different admin must approve this before it takes effect (Admin → Approvals).” and the toggle returns to its saved value. 3 → also only a request. After step 4 both flags change; the flag change log shows the reason with “(approved by a second admin)”.

cases.title: Business rules, commission rates and the registration fee wait for a second admin
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B; note the live default commission, registration fee and rule rbacV2.
cases.expected: Each call answers 202 with a pending approval: “Change setting rbacV2”, “Commission DEFAULT → 4.50%”, “Registration fee → ₹…”, “Reset setting rbacV2 to defaults”. Live rule, commission and fee are unchanged until step 6 (TC-FIN-001 / TC-ONB-021 apply at once only with the flag OFF); after approval each is applied as Admin A through the existing setter.

cases.title: With four-eye OFF every admin action applies at once, as before
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` OFF (production state).
cases.steps:
1. Set a role (TC-RBAC-009) and save privileges (TC-RBAC-010)
2. Revoke a role (TC-RBAC-013)
3. Suspend and reinstate a user (TC-RBAC-024, TC-ADM-018)
4. Change a feature flag with a reason
5. Set a commission rate (TC-FIN-001)
6. Open /admin/approvals
cases.expected: Every change applies immediately with the v1 results (200 / 201, no 202); no approval request is created; Admin → Approvals shows only the “Two-admin approval is off …” note and “Nothing waiting”.

cases.title: Bootstrap: the Super Admin approves alone while fewer than two admins are active
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; exactly one ACTIVE admin, and it is SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL (default ceo@agtci.com) — local database, or staging only with the owner's agreement; otherwise Blocked.
cases.steps:
1. Super Admin raises a change (e.g. privileges of a test user)
2. Open /admin/approvals
3. Click “Approve (single admin)” on own request
4. Read the audit log and the Super Admin's inbox
cases.expected: Warning “Fewer than two admins are active, so the Super Admin may approve alone. …”; the own card offers “Approve (single admin)” and “Cancel request”. Step 3 → “Approved as a single-admin approval (recorded and e-mailed to the Super Admin).”; the change applies; the decision is marked single-admin; audit action approval.single_admin; e-mail to SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL “GoKesari: single-admin approval — {title}” with request, type, reason, approver, IST time and “This mode switches off by itself once a second admin is active.”

cases.title: Bootstrap switches off with a second admin and never helps another admin
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON. Case A: two active admins. Case B: one active admin who is not SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL.
cases.steps:
1. Case A: the Super Admin raises a change and POSTs decide APPROVE on it
2. Case B: the only admin raises a change and POSTs decide APPROVE on it
cases.expected: 1 → 403 “A different admin must approve this request (two admins are active).” and no “Approve (single admin)” button. 2 → 403 “A different admin must approve this request.”. Nothing is applied.

cases.title: Emergency suspension applies at once and waits 24 h for a second admin
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` ON; Admin A and Admin B; a test customer signed in on a second browser.
cases.steps:
1. Admin A suspends the customer with the reason “QA emergency” (POST /api/users/{id}/suspend)
2. The customer loads any page
3. Admin B opens /admin/approvals
4. Admin B clicks “Confirm”
5. Developer moves confirm_by of a second such request into the past; reload
cases.expected: The suspension applies immediately — the customer is signed out on the next request as in TC-RBAC-024; the response carries approvalId and confirmBy (24 hours later); audit user.emergency_suspended. Card “Confirm emergency suspension” with the badge “Confirm by dd Mmm yyyy, hh:mm IST” and buttons “Confirm” / “Reject (lift suspension)”. Confirm → the user stays suspended. An unconfirmed request past its time shows the red badge “Confirmation overdue”.

cases.title: Rejecting the confirmation lifts the emergency suspension
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-031, a new emergency suspension by Admin A.
cases.steps:
1. Admin B clicks “Reject (lift suspension)” with no comment
2. Admin B types “Not needed” and clicks it again
3. The user signs in
cases.expected: 1 → “Say why you are rejecting.”. 2 → “Rejected.”; the user is ACTIVE again, reinstated with the reason “Emergency suspension not confirmed by a second admin: Not needed”. 3 → sign-in works.

cases.title: Accountant drafts and submits a balanced journal entry
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_accounting` ON (Admin → Feature flags; seeded OFF; ON on staging since 23-Nov). gk-ops acting as Accountant; the current month is open.
cases.steps:
1. Open /staff/accounting (Journals)
2. In “New journal entry” keep today's date, Narration “QA receipt”
3. Line 1: Code 1010, Account “QA bank”, Debit ₹1; Line 2: Code 4990, Account “QA income”, Credit ₹1
4. Click “Save draft”
5. Click “Submit” on the new draft
cases.expected: The running line reads “Debits ₹1.00 · Credits ₹1.00” in green. Save → “JE-xxxxxx saved as a draft.” and the entry is listed DRAFT, ₹1.00. Submit → status SUBMITTED with a “Withdraw” button; the CA's To approve tab lists “JE-xxxxxx: QA receipt (₹1.00)”. Audit fin_journal.drafted. The existing finance ledger is not written.

cases.title: Unbalanced and malformed entries are refused
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-033.
cases.steps:
1. Enter Debit ₹100 and Credit ₹90
2. Click “Save draft”
3. Enter both a debit and a credit on line 1 and save
4. POST /api/staff/accounting/journals with one line
5. POST with the narration “ab”
cases.expected: “Submit to CA” stays disabled while debits ≠ credits or both are zero. Step 2 → “The entry does not balance: debits ₹100.00, credits ₹90.00.” (422). Step 3 → “Line 1: enter a debit or a credit, not both and not neither.”. Steps 4–5 → 422 “Please check the highlighted fields.”. Nothing is saved.

cases.title: The CA posts the entry; the preparer can never approve it
cases.preconditions: A SUBMITTED entry below ₹50,000 from TC-STAFF-033; gk-oplim acting as CA; for step 4 a user who holds both Accountant and CA.
cases.steps:
1. As the Accountant POST /api/approvals/{request id}/decide {decision: APPROVE}
2. As CA open To approve and click “Approve”
3. As Accountant reload Journals
4. The dual-role user prepares an entry as Accountant, switches to CA and approves it
cases.expected: 1 → 403 “Only a CA can decide this request.”. 2 → “Approved and applied.” and the card leaves the list. 3 → the entry is POSTED; audit fin_journal.posted. 4 → 403 “You cannot approve your own request.”.

cases.title: CA rejects with a comment; the Accountant corrects, resubmits or withdraws
cases.preconditions: Two SUBMITTED entries from the Accountant.
cases.steps:
1. CA clicks “Reject” on entry 1 with no comment
2. CA rejects it with “Wrong account”
3. Accountant reads Journals
4. Accountant PUT /api/staff/accounting/journals/{id} with corrected lines, then clicks “Submit”
5. Accountant clicks “Withdraw” on entry 2
cases.expected: 1 → “Say why you are rejecting.”. 2 → “Rejected.”; entry 1 is REJECTED and shows “CA: Wrong account”. The list offers no edit or submit for a rejected entry (code_check); the PUT turns it back into a DRAFT and Submit sends it again. 5 → “Done.”; entry 2 is DRAFT again and its approval request CANCELLED.

cases.title: Entries of ₹50,000 or more need the CA and then a different admin
cases.preconditions: Rule rbacV2.highValueJournalPaise at its default 5,000,000 paise (₹50,000); Accountant, CA, admin; a user holding CA and Admin for step 6.
cases.steps:
1. Accountant submits an entry of ₹49,999.99
2. Accountant submits an entry of ₹50,000.00
3. CA approves both
4. Admin opens /admin/approvals
5. Admin approves the ₹50,000.00 entry
6. The dual-role user approves a high-value entry as CA, switches to Admin and approves it again
cases.expected: ₹49,999.99 → POSTED by the CA alone. ₹50,000.00 → after the CA it stays SUBMITTED, leaves the CA's list and appears on Admin → Approvals (stage 2); the CA's card nevertheless reads “Approved and applied.” (code_check). Admin Approve → POSTED. Step 6 → 403 “The CA who approved this cannot also activate it.”.

cases.title: Posted entries are final; a correction is a reversing entry
cases.preconditions: A POSTED entry; database access for the developer.
cases.steps:
1. Developer: UPDATE fin_journal_entries SET narration = 'x' WHERE id = '{posted}'; then DELETE it
2. Accountant clicks “Reverse” and gives the reason “Posted to wrong month”
3. Click “Reverse” again on the same entry
4. Submit the reversal draft; CA approves it
5. Open Trial balance
cases.expected: Step 1 fails: “fin_journal_entries: a posted entry is corrected by a reversing entry, never edited” / “… cannot be deleted”. Step 2 creates a DRAFT “Reversal of JE-xxxxxx: Posted to wrong month” with each debit and credit swapped (a reason under 5 characters is refused). Step 3 → “A reversal of this entry is already being prepared.”. After step 4 the original is REVERSED and the pair nets to zero in the trial balance.

cases.title: The CA (not the Accountant) closes and reopens a month; closed months take no entries
cases.preconditions: An entry SUBMITTED in 2026-11; CA and Accountant.
cases.steps:
1. Accountant opens Periods and POST /api/staff/accounting/periods/2026-11 {action: CLOSE}
2. CA clicks “Close period” on 2026-11
3. CA decides the waiting entry and closes again
4. Accountant saves a draft dated in 2026-11
5. CA clicks “Reopen” with “abc”, then with “Late invoice”
cases.expected: Accountant sees the periods with no Close button; the API → 403. Step 2 → “1 entry waits for approval in 2026-11. Decide them before closing.”. Step 3 → “2026-11 closed.” with the badge CLOSED and the time. Step 4 → “The period 2026-11 is closed. Ask the CA to reopen it, or date the entry in an open period.”. Reopen “abc” → “Say why the period is reopened.”; “Late invoice” → “2026-11 reopened.”. Audit fin_period.closed / fin_period.reopened.

cases.title: Trial balance and its CSV
cases.preconditions: Posted, reversed, draft and submitted entries exist.
cases.steps:
1. Open Trial balance
2. Click “Download CSV”
3. GET /api/staff/accounting/trial-balance?from=2026-11&to=2026-11&format=csv
cases.expected: Table Account / Debit / Credit / Balance with a Total row; total debit = total credit; only POSTED and REVERSED entries count. The download is trial-balance-start-now.csv with the header “Account code,Account name,Debit (INR),Credit (INR),Balance (INR)” and a “Total” row; step 3 limits it to 2026-11 (file trial-balance-2026-11-2026-11.csv).

cases.title: Accounting is closed to every other role
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_accounting` ON; Support User, Operations Manager and Customer accounts.
cases.steps:
1. As Support User open /staff/accounting
2. As Customer open /staff/accounting
3. As Support User GET /api/staff/accounting/trial-balance
4. As Operations Manager GET /api/staff/accounting/journals
cases.expected: Support User → /staff; Customer → /staff → /; steps 3–4 → 403 “You do not have permission to perform this action.”, each written as authz.denied. No journal, period or rate data is shown.

cases.title: Commission change: Accountant proposes, CA approves, admin activates
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_accounting` ON; Accountant, CA, admin; note the live default commission on /admin/finance.
cases.steps:
1. Accountant: Rates tab → “Propose a rate change”: “Default commission (%)”, New % 4.5, Effective from = now (IST), Reason “QA rate test”, click “Send to CA”
2. Check the default commission
3. CA approves it in To approve
4. Admin approves it on /admin/approvals
5. Check the Rates tab and the default commission
cases.expected: “Proposed. The CA approves it, then an admin activates it.”; row “Commission DEFAULT → 4.50%” with status PENDING_CA; the live rate is unchanged. After the CA → PENDING_ADMIN and Admin → Approvals shows “Commission DEFAULT → 4.50% from YYYY-MM-DD”. After the admin → ACTIVATED; the default commission is 450 bp, set through the existing setter with the note “Rate proposal …”; audit rate_proposal.activated.

cases.title: A future-dated rate is scheduled and activated by the hourly job
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-042 with Effective from tomorrow 10:00 IST.
cases.steps:
1. Propose, CA approves, admin approves
2. Check the rate before the time
3. After the time, let the hourly rbac-v2 job run (or the developer runs it)
4. Check the Rates tab and the rate
cases.expected: After the admin the proposal is SCHEDULED and the rate unchanged. The first hourly run after the effective time activates it (ACTIVATED, audit rate_proposal.activated); an activation error leaves it FAILED with the error. The job does nothing while `rbac_v2_accounting` is OFF.

cases.title: Registration-fee and delivery-charge proposals go through the existing setters
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-042; note the active registration fee and rule shopWallet.deliveryChargePaise.
cases.steps:
1. Propose “Registration fee (₹)” 1199 effective a future date
2. Propose “Delivery charge (₹)” 25 effective now
3. CA and admin approve both
4. Check the fee schedule and the delivery charge
cases.expected: Approval titles “Registration fee → ₹1199.00 from …” and “Delivery charge → ₹25.00 per delivery from …”. The fee is handed to the existing fee schedule on admin approval with effectiveFrom = the IST date (the fee service schedules a future date itself); the delivery charge sets shopWallet.deliveryChargePaise = 2500. Limits: fee up to ₹10,00,000, delivery charge up to ₹10,000.

cases.title: Rate proposals: who may propose, limits, rejection and withdrawal
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-042.
cases.steps:
1. As CA POST /api/staff/accounting/rates; as Admin A POST a proposal, let the CA approve it, then Admin A approves stage 2
2. As Accountant enter the reason “abc”
3. As Accountant propose 51%
4. CA rejects one proposal with a comment; admin rejects another at stage 2
5. Accountant POST /api/staff/accounting/rates/{id}/cancel on a waiting one
cases.expected: 1 → 403 for the CA. The admin's proposal is accepted (ADMIN holds every permission) but that admin cannot activate it at stage 2: 403 “A different admin must approve this request.” (Super Admin bootstrap excepted). 2 → “Send to CA” stays disabled (API 422). 3 → 422 “Please check the highlighted fields.” (rate above 5000 bp). 4 → REJECTED, rate untouched. 5 → CANCELLED (there is no cancel button on the screen).

cases.title: “Check file” reads a bank statement without saving it
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_accounting` ON; Accountant; CSV with the header “Date,Narration,Ref No,Debit,Credit,Balance”, an “Opening Balance” row and two transactions (credit ₹1.00, debit ₹0.50).
cases.steps:
1. Open /staff/accounting?tab=bank
2. In “Import a bank statement” choose the file
3. Click “Check file”
4. Look at the statement list
cases.expected: Summary “2 lines, {from} to {to}. Debits ₹0.50, credits ₹1.00.” plus opening and closing balances (or “The file has no balance column.”); no row problems; nothing is added to the list. “Import and match” is enabled once the account name has 3+ characters.

cases.title: Import matches by UTR and amount and suggests the rest
cases.preconditions: Records marked PAID: a shop payout ₹500 with UTR U1; a rider payout ₹300 two days before the line date; a payout ₹200 with UTR U3. Statement lines: debit ₹500 ref U1; debit ₹300 without a reference; debit ₹250 with U3 in the narration; credit ₹1,000.
cases.steps:
1. Name the account “QA current ••0000” and click “Import and match”
2. Open the statement
3. Click “Accept suggestion” on the ₹300 line
4. Open the ₹250 line
cases.expected: “BS-xxxxxx imported: 1 matched automatically, 2 with a suggestion, 1 to match by hand.”. ₹500 → “MATCHED (auto)” → the shop payout. ₹300 → “Suggested: … Same amount, recorded on …; no bank reference to confirm it.” and Accept → “Line n matched.”. ₹250 → “The reference agrees but the amount differs: bank ₹250.00, record ₹200.00.” with no Accept button. The ₹1,000 credit is never matched to a payout. Payout, refund and settlement tables are only read.

cases.title: Statement import refusals
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-046; one statement already imported for “QA current ••0000”.
cases.steps:
1. Check and import a file with the date 31/02/2026 on one row
2. Import the already imported file again
3. Import another file for “QA current ••0000” whose dates overlap
4. Use the account name “HDFC 12345678”
5. Upload a .pdf, an empty file and a file over 10 MB
6. Import the overlapping file under another account name
cases.expected: 1 → Check file lists “Row n: “31/02/2026” is not a date (use DD/MM/YYYY).” and import → 422 “1 row has a problem; nothing was imported. Fix the file and upload it again.”. 2 → 409 “This file was already imported as BS-xxxxxx.”. 3 → 409 “BS-xxxxxx already covers {from} to {to} for this account. Import only the dates after it, or delete BS-xxxxxx first if it is still open.”. 4 → 422 “Use only the last 4 digits of the account number in its name, e.g. “HDFC current ••1234”.”. 5 → “Upload the bank statement as .csv or .xlsx (save an .xls or PDF statement as one of these first).”, “Choose the bank statement file (.csv or .xlsx).”, “The file is larger than 10 MB. Split the statement by month.”. 6 → imported.

cases.title: Manual matching rules
cases.preconditions: An OPEN statement with an unmatched debit ₹250, an unmatched credit and an unmatched debit ₹500; a PAID payout ₹200; a draft journal; a payout already matched on BS-000001.
cases.steps:
1. “Find match / exclude” on ₹250 and “Match” the ₹200 payout
2. Match the credit line to a payout (POST action match, kind SHOP_PAYOUT)
3. Match the credit to the draft journal
4. Exclude ₹500 with the reason “fee”
5. Match ₹500 to the payout already matched on BS-000001
6. Exclude ₹500 with “Bank charges”, then click “Undo”
cases.expected: 1 → “The amounts differ: bank ₹250.00, record ₹200.00. Record the difference with a journal entry and match the line to it, or exclude the line with a reason.”. 2 → “Money received is matched to a posted journal entry (record the receipt as a journal first).”. 3 → 404 “Journal entry (it must be marked paid, or the journal entry posted) was not found.”. 4 → “Say why this line needs no match (e.g. bank charges, interest).”. 5 → 409 “This shop payout is already matched to line n of BS-000001.”. 6 → EXCLUDED, then “Line n is unmatched again.”.

cases.title: Match, exclude, submit; the CA signs off and the statement is final
cases.preconditions: The statement of TC-STAFF-046 imported; the ₹1.00 journal of TC-STAFF-033 POSTED; Accountant and CA.
cases.steps:
1. Match the ₹1.00 credit to the posted journal
2. Exclude the ₹0.50 debit with “QA bank SMS charges”
3. Click “Submit to CA”
4. Try “Match again” via POST …/auto-match
5. CA approves it in To approve
6. “Download CSV”
7. Accountant DELETE /api/staff/accounting/bank-statements/{id}
cases.expected: Counts “1 matched · 1 excluded · 0 unmatched”; Submit → “Sent to the CA for sign-off.”, status SUBMITTED; step 4 → 409 “This statement is with the CA. Withdraw it to change it.”. CA Approve → RECONCILED; audit fin_bank_statement.reconciled. CSV BS-xxxxxx-reconciliation.csv starts “line,date,value_date,description,reference,debit_inr,credit_inr,balance_inr,status,matched_to,note”. Step 7 → 409 “This statement is reconciled and final.”; the database also refuses edits (“fin_bank_statements: a reconciled statement is final”).

cases.title: Sign-off refusals, send back, withdraw and delete
cases.preconditions: OPEN statements: one with an unmatched line, one whose balances leave a ₹10.00 gap; a second Accountant.
cases.steps:
1. POST …/submit on the statement with the unmatched line
2. Match everything on the ₹10.00-gap statement and submit
3. Submit a complete one; CA rejects it with “Recheck line 3”
4. Submit it again and click “Withdraw”
5. The second Accountant tries to submit or delete it
6. Click “Delete” on an OPEN statement and confirm
cases.expected: 1 → 409 “1 line is still unmatched. Match or exclude every line first.” (button disabled on screen). 2 → 409 “Opening balance + credits − debits differs from the closing balance by ₹10.00. A line is missing from the file.”. 3 → OPEN again with “Sent back by the CA: Recheck line 3”. 4 → “Withdrawn; you can change it again.”. 5 → 403 “Only the Accountant who imported this statement …”. 6 → confirm text “Delete BS-xxxxxx? Its matches are released; you can import the file again.”; it disappears and the same file imports and matches again.

cases.title: “Paid, not in bank” lists payouts missing from the statement
cases.preconditions: A payout marked PAID within the statement's dates that is on no statement line.
cases.steps:
1. Open the statement
2. Click the filter “Paid, not in bank”
3. Match the payout on another statement and reload
cases.expected: The payout is listed with amount, label, date and reference. When nothing is missing: “Nothing missing” / “Every payout and refund recorded as paid in these dates is on a bank statement.”. Filters All, Unmatched, Matched, Excluded show their lines.

cases.title: Bank reconciliation is for the Accountant (prepare) and the CA (view and sign off)
cases.preconditions: CA, Support User; `rbac_v2_accounting` ON, then OFF.
cases.steps:
1. As CA POST /api/staff/accounting/bank-statements with a file
2. As CA open the Bank tab and a statement
3. As Support User GET /api/staff/accounting/bank-statements
4. Flag OFF: as Accountant open the Bank tab and GET the list
cases.expected: 1 → 403; the CA's Bank tab has no import card and no match / exclude buttons, only the list, the lines and the CSV. 3 → 403. 4 → /staff/accounting redirects to /staff and the API answers 404 “This feature is not available.”.

cases.title: Admin → Staff teams: add and remove members
cases.preconditions: Admin; at least one user acting as Support Manager and one as Support User; same for Operations.
cases.steps:
1. Open Settings → Staff teams (/admin/staff-teams)
2. On “Support — {manager}” pick a member in “Add a member…” and click “Add”
3. Click “Remove” next to a member
4. Add someone already in another manager's team
5. Open the page as a non-admin
cases.expected: One card per manager (“Support — …”, “Operations — …”); “Added.” / “Removed.”; audit staff_team.changed; step 4 moves the member to the new manager. With no managers: “Give someone the Support Manager or Operations Manager role first (Users → privileges).”. Non-admin → /. Only people acting in the role right now are listed — a person holding it as a grant is missing (code_check).

cases.title: A team member or manager may hold the role as a grant (PR #493)
cases.preconditions: gk-ops holds Operations Manager and Support Manager as grants while acting as Accountant; gk-oplim holds Operations User and Support User while acting as Operator (Limited); a customer account.
cases.steps:
1. Admin POST /api/staff/teams {team: OPERATIONS, managerUserId: gk-ops, memberUserId: gk-oplim}
2. Same with team SUPPORT
3. Admin adds the customer as a SUPPORT member
4. gk-ops (acting as Support Manager) adds a member to another manager's team
cases.expected: Steps 1–2 → 201 (before #493: 422 “The manager must hold the OPERATIONS_MANAGER role.”). Step 3 → 422 “The member must hold the SUPPORT_USER role.”. Step 4 → 403 “Only an admin or the team's own manager can change a team.”.

cases.title: Support Manager dashboard and team workload
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_support` ON (seeded OFF; ON on staging since 23-Nov); Support Manager with two team members and tickets in several states.
cases.steps:
1. Open /staff/support (Dashboard)
2. Compare the counts with the queue
3. Open it as a Support User
4. Open it as a Support Manager with an empty team
cases.expected: Tiles New, Assigned, In progress, Pending / on hold, Awaiting shop owner, Resolved, Overdue (red when above 0) and “Avg. resolution (30 days)”; “Workload per Support User” lists only this manager's team with Open, Awaiting owner, Overdue, Resolved 7 d, Avg h. The Support User has no Dashboard or Queue tab (the service refuses with “Only a Support Manager sees the team dashboard.”). Empty team: “No Support Users in your team yet. …”.

cases.title: Queue: assign, priority SLA, side status and due date
cases.preconditions: As TC-STAFF-056; a NORMAL ticket raised by staff.
cases.steps:
1. Queue tab: assign the ticket to a team member
2. Set priority URGENT
3. Set the side status “On Hold”
4. Lower the priority to LOW
5. PATCH /api/staff/support/tickets/{id} {dueAt: a time after the current due time}
6. As Support User PATCH the same ticket
cases.expected: Each change → “Saved.”; the assignee gets “Ticket {n} assigned to you” and the badge reads “Assigned”. URGENT → due = received + 4 h (rule rbacV2.slaHoursByPriority: LOW 120 h, NORMAL 48 h, HIGH 24 h, URGENT 4 h), never after the statutory help-desk deadline; lowering the priority never moves the due time later. Badge “On Hold” (also “Pending Information”, “Rejected”). 5 → 422 “A due date cannot be later than the ticket's statutory deadline.”. 6 → 403.

cases.title: A ticket can go to someone who holds Support User as a grant (PR #500)
cases.preconditions: gk-oplim holds Support User but is acting as Operations User; gk-ops acting as Support Manager; a ticket; a customer and a deleted account.
cases.expected: 1 → assigned (before #500: 422 “Assign the ticket to a support team member, an operator or an administrator.”). 2 → the picker lists people acting in or holding Operator, Admin, Support Manager or Support User — a grant holder labelled “(staff)” — and never a deleted account. 3 → 422 “Assign the ticket to a support team member, an operator or an administrator.”.

cases.title: A Support User works only the tickets assigned to them
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_support` and `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests` ON; Support User with one assigned ticket on shop A; a ticket assigned to someone else on shop B.
cases.steps:
1. Open My work → My tickets
2. Open the assigned ticket (/admin/support/{id}) and “Open shop workbench →”
3. Open /admin/support/{other ticket}
4. Open /staff/support/shop/{shopB}?ticket={own ticket} and /staff/support/shop/{shopA} without a ticket
5. POST /api/staff/shops/{shopB}/changes with the other ticket's id, and with no ticket id
cases.expected: My tickets lists only tickets assigned to this user; the assigned ticket opens without an assignee picker; the workbench shows shop details and products (no bank details). The other ticket and both workbench URLs show the not-found page. Step 5 → 403 “This ticket is not assigned to you.” and 403 “Open the shop from a ticket assigned to you.”.

cases.title: Overdue tickets alert the Support Manager once
cases.preconditions: `rbac_v2_support` ON; a live ticket whose due time the developer moves into the past.
cases.steps:
1. Let the hourly rbac-v2 job run twice
2. Read the Support Manager's notifications and the dashboard
cases.expected: The ticket's manager (or every user acting as Support Manager when it has none) gets “Overdue: ticket {n}” with the IST due time, once per due time; the dashboard's Overdue count includes it. No alert while `rbac_v2_support` is OFF.

cases.title: Support proposes shop and price changes; nothing applies until the owner decides
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests` ON (seeded OFF; ON on staging since 23-Nov); Support User with an assigned ticket on shop A.
cases.steps:
1. Open the shop workbench from My tickets
2. Change the shop Description and one product's online price
3. Enter a reason and click “Send to the shop owner”
4. Check the live shop page and price
5. Send again with every value equal to today's
cases.expected: Alert “Nothing you change here is applied until the shop owner approves it. …”. Step 3 → “2 changes to {shop} sent to the shop owner. Nothing changes until they approve.”; the ticket becomes “Awaiting Shop Owner”; the owner is told “Changes to your shop need your approval” (link /shop/changes); “Waiting for the owner (1)” shows both items as “Waiting for the owner”. The live shop and price are unchanged. Step 5 → “Nothing changed.” (API: “Every proposed value is the same as the shop's current one.”).

cases.title: The shop owner decides item by item
cases.preconditions: The request of TC-STAFF-061 pending; shop A's owner.
cases.steps:
1. Open Price updates → Pending changes (/shop/changes)
2. Set the description item to Reject with no comment and click “Save my decisions”
3. Enter “Keep the old text” in “Why? (required)” and save
4. Open History
cases.expected: Title “Pending changes for approval”, tabs “Waiting for me” / “History”; the card shows “Proposed by … · decide by … IST”, the reason and What / Now / Proposed / Your decision. Step 2 → “Write why you reject (a comment is required for every rejected item).”. Step 3 → “Saved. Approved items are live now.”: the price is live, the description unchanged; History shows PARTIALLY APPROVED with the comment; the ticket moves to In Progress; the Support User is told “Shop owner decided on your changes” (“…: 1 applied, 1 rejected.”).

cases.title: Approve all resolves the ticket; MRP is the shop's own with append-only history
cases.preconditions: Support proposes “MRP (this shop only)” and an online price for one product; shop owner; database access.
cases.steps:
1. Owner clicks “Approve all”
2. Check the product in the shop and its master product MRP
3. Read shop_mrp_history
4. Developer runs UPDATE and DELETE on that history row
cases.expected: Both items apply through the owner's own writers (price ≤ MRP and other shop rules still enforced); the ticket becomes Resolved (an Operations raiser is told “… resolved — please confirm”). shop_mrp_history has a row with previous and new MRP, source CHANGE_REQUEST and the approval id; the master MRP is unchanged. Step 4 fails: “shop_mrp_history is append-only: UPDATE is not allowed” / “… DELETE …”.

cases.title: Proposal refusals: price above MRP, protected fields and bad values
cases.preconditions: Support User with an assigned ticket on shop A; a product with MRP ₹120.
cases.steps:
1. Propose online price ₹150 for the product
2. Propose field gstin for the shop
3. Propose pincode 012345 and contact phone 12345
4. Propose adding a product the shop already sells
cases.expected: 1 → 422 “{product}: online selling price ₹150.00 is above the MRP ₹120.00.”. 2 → 422 “Please check the highlighted fields.” (GSTIN and PAN are not proposable; they change only through government verification). 3 → “PIN code: 6 digits, not starting with 0.” and “Contact phone: a 10-digit Indian mobile number.”. 4 → “That product is already in the shop: propose a price change instead.”. Nothing is created.

cases.title: Only the shop's owner decides a change request
cases.preconditions: A pending change request for shop A; owner of shop B; Support User; Admin; a customer with no shop.
cases.steps:
1. Shop B's owner POST /api/approvals/{id}/decide {decision: APPROVE}
2. The Support User who proposed it does the same
3. An admin does the same
4. The customer opens /shop/changes; a guest opens it
5. With `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests` OFF the owner opens /shop/changes
cases.expected: 1–3 → 403 “Only the shop owner can decide this request.”; nothing applied. 4 → the customer is sent to /shop, the guest to /signin. 5 → /shop, and no “Pending changes” entry under Price updates (the decide API itself does not re-check the flag — code_check).

cases.title: A proposal the owner has since changed is superseded, never applied
cases.preconditions: Support proposed a new shop description; the owner then edits the description in the shop settings.
cases.steps:
1. Owner opens /shop/changes
2. Owner approves the item
3. On another request, let the hourly rbac-v2 job run after the owner's own edit
cases.expected: The item shows “You changed this since it was proposed.”. Approving does not overwrite the owner's text: the item becomes SUPERSEDED (“The shop changed this value after it was proposed.”). The hourly job marks stale pending items SUPERSEDED and tells the Support User “Proposed change superseded”; when every item is superseded the request is SUPERSEDED and an Awaiting Shop Owner ticket returns to In Progress.

cases.title: Reminders at 24 h and 72 h; expiry after 7 days
cases.preconditions: A pending change request linked to a ticket; the developer moves requested_at / expires_at back; rule rbacV2 reminderHours [24, 72], expiryDays 7.
cases.steps:
1. At 25 h run the hourly job twice
2. At 73 h run it
3. Past 7 days run it
4. The owner then tries to approve
cases.expected: One reminder “Changes to your shop still need your approval” at 24 h and one at 72 h, never repeated. After 7 days: request and items EXPIRED, nothing applied, the ticket gets the side status “Pending Information”; Support Managers and the Support User are told “Shop change request expired”. Step 4 → 409 “This request has already been decided.”; deciding after 7 days but before the job has run → 409 “This request has expired.”. Nothing is applied either way.

cases.title: Bulk price list from the shop's template
cases.preconditions: Support User on the workbench of an assigned shop with several products.
cases.steps:
1. Click “Download this shop's template (CSV)”
2. Change one product's online price, set another's above its MRP, add a row with an unknown shop_product_id
3. Upload it in “Bulk price list”
4. Click “Download the error report”
cases.expected: Template header “shop_product_id,product_name,barcode,online_price_inr,offline_price_inr,mrp_inr,available” filled with today's values. Upload → “4 rows read: 1 change(s) sent to the owner in one request; 2 row(s) with problems.” (counts follow the file). Error report price-list-errors.csv “row,shop_product_id,problem” with “Online price ₹… is above the MRP ₹….” and “Not a product of this shop (keep the shop_product_id from the template).”. The good rows form one change request with one item per field.

cases.title: A master-data correction goes to an admin
cases.preconditions: Support User; a master product; admin.
cases.steps:
1. POST /api/staff/master-data {productId, field: hsnCode, proposedValue, reason: “Wrong HSN on pack”}
2. Support User POST /api/approvals/{id}/decide APPROVE
3. Admin approves it on /admin/approvals
4. Check the master product
cases.expected: 1 → 201, request “Master data: {product} — hsnCode”. 2 → 403 “Only an admin can decide this request.”. 3 → “Approved and applied.”: the decision is recorded only — the master product is unchanged until the admin edits it in Product master.

cases.title: Upload documents and versions; the file type is read from the bytes
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_support` ON; Support User on the workbench of an assigned shop; a PDF, an .exe renamed .pdf, an 11 MB PDF; rule documentUpload.maxUploadBytes at its default 10,000,000 bytes.
cases.steps:
1. In “Documents” choose type FSSAI licence, title “FSSAI 2026”, upload the PDF
2. Upload a new version with “New version”
3. Upload the renamed .exe
4. Upload the 11 MB file
5. Developer runs UPDATE on staff_document_versions
cases.expected: “Saved as version 1.” then “Saved as version 2.”; both versions listed with IST upload time; a new version resets the badge to UNVERIFIED. 3 → “Upload a PDF, JPEG, PNG or WebP file, or a price list as .csv / .xlsx.”. 4 → “A file can be at most 10.0 MB.” (docs say 5 MB — code_check). 5 fails: “staff_document_versions: a version is never changed; upload a new one”. Audit staff_document.uploaded.

cases.title: Who verifies and who sees a shop's documents
cases.preconditions: Documents on shop A; Support Manager, Support User (assigned to shop A), another Support User, shop A's owner, shop B's owner.
cases.steps:
1. Support Manager clicks “Verify”, then “Reject” on another document
2. Support User POST /api/staff/documents/{id}/verify
3. Shop A's owner GET /api/staff/documents?shopId={A}
4. Shop B's owner and the unassigned Support User GET the same
5. The unassigned Support User uploads to shop A
cases.expected: 1 → badges VERIFIED / REJECTED, audit staff_document.verified. 2 → 403 “Only a Support Manager or admin verifies documents.”. 3 → the list with versions. 4 → 403 “You cannot see this shop's documents.”. 5 → 403 “You cannot add documents to this shop.”.

cases.title: Downloads only through a signed link that expires after 10 minutes
cases.preconditions: A document version; the Support User who may see it; a second signed-out browser.
cases.steps:
1. Click a version to download it
2. Copy the /api/staff/documents/file?t=… link and open it signed out within 10 minutes
3. Open it again after 10 minutes
4. Change one character of the token
cases.expected: 1 → downloads as an attachment with Cache-Control “no-store, private” and X-Content-Type-Options “nosniff”; audit staff_document.link_issued. 2 → works without a session. 3 and 4 → 404 “Document was not found.”.

cases.title: Deleting a document needs two admins
cases.preconditions: A document with 2 versions; Support Manager; Admin A and Admin B.
cases.steps:
1. Support Manager POST /api/staff/documents/{id}/delete {reason: “Duplicate upload”}
2. Admin A does the same
3. Admin A approves own request
4. Admin B approves it
5. GET /api/staff/documents?shopId=…
cases.expected: 1 → 403 “You do not have access to this area.”. 2 → 202, request “Delete document “{title}” (2 versions)” (there is no delete button on the screen). 3 → 403. 4 → “Approved and applied.”: the versions' bytes are removed and the document is marked DELETED (no longer listed); audit staff_document.deleted.

cases.title: Operations Manager assigns a task; the Operations User works it
cases.preconditions: Flag `rbac_v2_operations` ON (seeded OFF; ON on staging since 23-Nov); gk-ops acting as Operations Manager with gk-oplim in its Operations team, acting as Operations User; shop A.
cases.steps:
1. Manager: Tasks tab → “New task”: Kind Follow-up, Assign to gk-oplim, Title “QA follow up with the shop”, Priority Normal, Due (IST), Shop (optional) shop A → “Assign task”
2. Operations User reads notifications and opens My tasks
3. Open the task, click “Start”, add a note with “Add note”, “Set follow-up”
